scenario: A chess federation certifies arbiters who demonstrate comprehensive rulebook mastery OR strong interpersonal dispute-resolution skill. Both competencies are independent in the candidate pool; OR-gate certification produces negative within-certified-group correlation.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (rulebook mastery) OR (dispute-resolution skill)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(rule_mastery | ¬dispute_resolution, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(rule_mastery | dispute_resolution, selected) and show it equals P(rule_mastery). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between rulebook mastery and dispute-resolution skill.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks dispute-resolution skill must possess rulebook mastery to be admitted — hence P(rule_mastery|¬dispute_resolution,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has dispute-resolution skill is admitted regardless of rulebook mastery, so P(rule_mastery|dispute_resolution,sel)=P(rule_mastery)=0.35. The gap (1.0 vs 0.35) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between rulebook mastery and dispute-resolution skill observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.35+0.55-0.35×0.55=0.7075. (2) Among candidates without dispute-resolution skill: only those with rulebook mastery are selected → P(rule_mastery|¬dispute_resolution,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with dispute-resolution skill: selected regardless of rulebook mastery → P(rule_mastery|dispute_resolution,sel)=P(rule_mastery)=0.35. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬dispute_resolution raises P(rule_mastery) from 0.35 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.35,0.55
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.7075)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.35)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
